post.caption: Dorothy's ruby slippers had no rubies. In the book, Dorothy's magic shoes are silver, but the 1939 film made them red so they would stand out on the yellow brick road. They began as plain white silk pumps from the Innes Shoe Company, dyed red and covered in sequins. The sequins had to be dark red because bright red looked orange in Technicolor. MGM made several pairs and only four film pairs are known to survive. The Smithsonian's pair has been in its collection since 1979. For the film's fiftieth anniversary, a Winston jewelry firm made a pair with real rubies and diamonds in size four.
